closest.why: First journal statement: Berglund, Hübsch, Minic, LHEP 2021, 186 (arXiv 29 Oct 2020). The abstract says dark matter 'comes from the degrees of freedom dual to the visible matter'; the text proposes that 'the dual sector ... should be interpreted as the dark matter sector', with x̃ spanning 'the canonically conjugate dual space' ([x, x̃] = 2πiλ²) and the dual-matter Lagrangian beside ours on √−g(x). Same identification. The sectors are 'mixed/correlated' (a correlation that 'becomes invisible in effective field theory'), not coupled through gravity only.

Earliest written statement found: Minic, proceedings of the 10th Mathematical Physics Meeting, Belgrade (2020), pp. 183–218, arXiv 29 Feb 2020, from a talk at the September 2019 meeting whose content is unknown. §5 writes the Standard Model Lagrangian and 'their duals (that could be interpreted as dark matter Lagrangian', both on g(x) after the x̃ integral. It says the dual quanta 'should be detectable through their particular metaparticle entanglement to visible matter', the opposite of C1's permanent null. Its conclusion asks whether Born reciprocity is 'a criterion for vacuum selection' that picks 'Standard Model and its dual, describing the dark matter sector'. That is a symmetric selection, not a broken one.

Closest in polarization language: Hübsch and Minic 2024, arXiv preprint. The spacetime label x 'corresponds to a choice of (classical spacetime) polarization in modular (quantum) spacetime'. Dual fields φ̃, the backgrounds of the dual momentum p̃, are the 'dark matter' fields, 'fuzzy' because they do not commute with the visible ones. It restates 2003.00318 and 2010.15610 (arXiv:2610.19522, 14 Oct 2026, repeats it), with no spontaneous breaking, no gate and no monopoles.

Snowmass contribution (arXiv 14 Feb 2022, preprint) co-signed by Freidel, Leigh and Kowalski-Glikman with Berglund, Hübsch, Mattingly and Minic: each quantum field has a 'dual', which 'could be associated with dark matter degrees of freedom'. Hedged (partial), it shows that the metastring circle beyond Minic's group had endorsed the association by February 2022.

For the polarization part only: Freidel, Leigh, Minic, JHEP 06 (2015) 006, already #11's [26S]. 'if all probes agree on what we mean by space-time, then we have broken Born duality — there is a preferred choice of polarization, the space-time one.' The full text has no 'spontaneous' and no 'dark matter'. #11 §3 credits the idea to FLM and claims the spontaneous reading, with η as order parameter, as the program's own.

For the coupling only: Foot's 2014 review (journal) of mirror dark matter, an exact copy of the Standard Model 'interacting with the known particles predominantly via gravity', citing Lee–Yang 1956 and Kobzarev–Okun–Pomeranchuk 1966. The mirror is space-time parity, and halos need kinetic mixing ε ~ 10⁻⁹, which predicts direct-detection signals; strict P4 allows ε ≲ 10⁻¹³ and predicts none. Bimetric versions: Hossenfelder 2008 (0807.2838), twin fields that 'only interact gravitationally' but repel; Aoki and Maeda 2014 (1312.7040), twin matter on the second metric of ghost-free bigravity as the dark-matter term.

For the χ form's observable only: halo fits prefer a mildly velocity-dependent self-interaction, σ/m ≈ 2 cm²/g on galaxy scales falling to ≈ 0.1 cm²/g on cluster scales. With Sagunski et al. 2021 (2006.12515, clusters 0.19 ± 0.09 cm²/g), this weighs mildly against 'zero cluster signal'. With resonant SIDM (1810.04709), it shows that a dwarf-strong, cluster-weak knee has ordinary mechanisms. No paper gates a self-interaction by relative velocity through momentum-space locality.

conjectures.new_in_conjecture: The literature found does not state the identification inside spontaneously broken reciprocity: conjugate matter as the matter of the polarization our vacuum did not select, sealed off by P4 so that it couples to ours only through gravity (and X) and direct detection stays null for good. The metastring school's dual sector is instead correlated with visible matter and expected to be detectable. Neither of C1's two forms is published: no paper gates a dark-matter self-interaction by relative velocity through momentum-space locality (the knee alone has ordinary routes, Yukawa and resonant SIDM), and no paper proposes monopoles, or any dark matter, localized in momentum (C1 and C2 not-found statements). Separately, a gravity-coupled copy of ordinary matter (mirror and twin matter) and a preferred polarization that breaks Born duality (FLM 2015) are published; their combination with the identification is not.
conjectures.published_parts: The identification itself is published by D. Minic and collaborators in metastring theory: dark matter as the dual, Born-reciprocal counterpart of the Standard Model, one dual partner per particle, gravitating in our spacetime. It was first written in Minic's Belgrade proceedings (arXiv 29 Feb 2020, from a September 2019 talk of unknown content), first stated in a journal by Berglund, Hübsch and Minic (arXiv 29 Oct 2020; LHEP 2021, in the abstract), and restated by the same group in eight further papers to 14 Oct 2026. Freidel, Leigh and Kowalski-Glikman co-signed a hedged form in February 2022, and a 2022 Prog. Part. Nucl. Phys. review relays it. These statements precede P.R.'s first written statement (lab notebook v0.1, September 2026, unpublished) by 6.5–6.6 years, the journal one by 5.8–5.9 years. The record already cites one of the anticipating papers (Berglund–Hübsch–Minic, IJMPD 32, 2330002 (2023), arXiv:2212.06086) for its dual-spacetime cosmological constant, without comparing its dark-matter claim.

notes: Lens: scope and chronology. Read: BRIEF.md; panel/C1.json in full, with results.json for the truncated related summaries; #11 §1, §3, §4, §8, §9, §12, §13 row 7, App. A item 4; the two wiki pages; notes/broken-born-theory.md (v0.1 header, §9 row 7); panel/C2.json (the monopole form). Passages I read myself with lit.py: 2003.00318 §5 and conclusion, 2010.15610, 1502.08005, 2407.06207 §3.2–3.3, 2305.12593, 2205.02787, gr-qc/0608086, 1401.3965; quotes re-checked for 0807.2838, 1312.7040, 1508.03339, 2006.12515. Dates are arXiv v1 dates from the tool's cache. The intervals were computed in panel/c1-scope/intervals.py; the reading log is panel/c1-scope/reading-log.txt. How 'anticipated' must be qualified. (1) Scope: it covers the identification only, P.R.'s 'dark matter is conjugate (momentum) matter'. Nothing in the evidence states the χ form's velocity gate, the monopole form, strict P4's gravity-only coupling with its permanent null, or the spontaneous-breaking reading. A record that says 'anticipated' should name the published part and the new parts together. (2) Physics: the school's dual sector is correlated with visible matter through non-gravitational (Berry-phase-like) terms and the acceleration scale of modified dark matter. Minic 2020 says its quanta 'should be detectable through their particular metaparticle entanglement to visible matter', the opposite of #11 §13 row 7. 'Anticipated' means the idea is published, not that the program's dark matter is the school's. (3) Source: all ten 'anticipates' findings come from one group (Minic with Berglund, Hübsch, Edmonds, Takeuchi and others) and restate one proposal. arXiv flags text overlap for 2109.12763 (with 2003.00318) and 2407.06207 (with 2307.16712). No statement independent of that group was found (not-found statements 3–5). Precursors, related only: Finkelstein (arXiv 2006, IJTP 2008), who says the momentum coordinates of events contribute 'possibly to dark matter'; Chang, Minic, Sun and Takeuchi 2016, non-local excitations extended in space and momentum; FLM 2017, an expectation only; Edmonds et al. 2017, metaparticles as quanta of modified dark matter. (4) Chronology: the earliest written statement is dated 29 Feb 2020 (conference proceedings). The Belgrade talk of September 2019 (INSPIRE cnum C19-09-09.8) has unknown content. FLM, IJMPA 34, 1941004 (2019), is not on arXiv and could not be read; its INSPIRE abstract mentions metaparticles but not dark matter. So the date is 'no later than 29 Feb 2020'. The first journal statement is LHEP 2021 (arXiv 29 Oct 2020). Hübsch–Minic arXiv:2610.19522 (14 Oct 2026) is later than P.R.'s September 2026 notebook, and earlier than his public wiki (serving at comatter.science by 22–26 Oct 2026) only by 8–12 days. Do not list it as prior to his first statement. (5) The g1 verifier's 'what C1 adds is ... not the null itself' (not-found statement 5) goes too far. The literature explains the null so far by non-locality (Chang et al. 2016; Minic 2020) but still expects a detection, through entanglement. A permanent null with a kill condition is not stated together with the identification. As a property of gravity-only dark matter in general it is generic: Hossenfelder 2008's twin fields 'only interact gravitationally'. (6) 'Organized around momentum' does not separate the two. After the reduction, the school's dual fields and C1's χ both live on the spacetime metric (χ is 'x-clumping', App. A item 4). Only the monopole form would localize dark matter in momentum, and no paper does. (7) Labels: none disputed. I checked the single-agent 'anticipates' on 2305.12593: the quote is FOUND, in a parenthetical citing BHM 2020 that is worded like 2212.06086's 'good candidates'. I agree with 'related' for Sheng Ran (dark matter 'is not a new particle species'; a removed, non-reviewed preprint of Dec 2025, after the school in any case), for Pavšič 2022 (a quaternionic doubling of the field, not the position–momentum polarization) and for FKLM 2021 (hedged between dark energy and dark matter). (8) Fixes to carry. 2011.08852's authors are Jejjala, Kavic, Minic and Takeuchi (INSPIRE), not C.-H. Tze. 2305.12593 is Bulg. J. Phys. 51, 060 (2024) per Crossref; INSPIRE lists it as a conference paper (BASIC 2023 proceedings). The summaries of 2610.19522 and 2111.05659 open with 'Outside this list's named conjectures (C5–C7)', a triage artifact: both are C1 findings.
